key_insight: This paper shows that large language models can be used to invent optimization algorithms, not just solve optimization tasks. The key idea is to build a verified problem contract and then evolve a set of complementary heuristics that work together on cases where any single method falls short.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of designing robust combinatorial optimization algorithms that can handle diverse problem instances, especially when one heuristic alone cannot solve all cases well.
method: Create a verified problem contract that clearly defines the optimization task and constraints.
Use a large language model framework called LACE to generate and improve candidate heuristics.
Evolve a portfolio of complementary heuristics so different methods cover each other’s weaknesses.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a new pathway for automating algorithm design in combinatorial optimization. It can reduce manual heuristic engineering and improve performance by combining multiple specialized strategies instead of relying on a single solver.

paper_title: Large language models discover complementary heuristics for combinatorial optimization
paper_authors: Huatian Gong, Shuaian Wang, Dongping Song, Jiuh-Biing Sheu, Ran Yan
